subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` credential-shaped names bypass the generic sensitive-name block for the active skill's host run, and what isolation boundary prevents unrelated exec leakage?
rationale: The bug is source-reproducible and contradicts documented host-run skill env behavior, but the fix intentionally changes how credentials reach executable subprocess environments and overlaps an inverse secret-leak issue.

options.title: Admit scoped active-skill env secrets
options.body: Permit only explicitly configured keys for the active intended skill path, keep dangerous host env names blocked, and add tests for selected-skill delivery plus unrelated exec isolation.

options.title: Keep metadata-only sensitive allowlist
options.body: Require skills to declare every credential-shaped env name in metadata and update docs or doctor guidance so arbitrary `skills.entries.*.env` credential names are not promised.

options.title: Defer to a new secret contract
options.body: Leave the sanitizer unchanged until maintainers define a SecretRef or plugin-owned credential path for CLI skills that need headless auth.

recommendation.title: Admit scoped active-skill env secrets
recommendation.body: Permit only explicitly configured keys for the active intended skill path, keep dangerous host env names blocked, and add tests for selected-skill delivery plus unrelated exec isolation.

likelyOwner.reason: This owner has recent adjacent history on the skill env and release/current-main path, with co-authorship on the active env stripping work.
